To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
triterpens and sterols from oil-soluble rice bran extract lower diet-induced GIP release and prevent obesity in mice.
triterpne alcohols and phytosterols from rice bran prevent obesity by increasing fatty oxidation in muscles and suppressing fatty acid synthesis in liver through GIP and GIP-independent mechanism.
triterpens and sterols from a natural food, rice bran, prevent diet-induced obesity by suppressing postprandial secretion of GIP and by regulating fatty acid metabolism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the bioactive constituents of rice bran oil, and their mechanism of action on energy metabolism.
the identification of food-derived GIP modulators and their application for the development of foods to prevent obesity.
the development of foods containing rice bran components that can help prevent obesity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rice bran oil-soluble component TASP prevents diet-induced obesity by suppressing GIP secretion and increasing fatty acid oxidation.
the rice bran triterpenoids and sterols are effective in lowering postprandial plasma GIP levels, and that this effect is associated with the prevention of diet-induced obesity in rodents.
rice bran oil and its triterpene components are effective at preventing diet-induced obesity and improving glucose metabolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
triterpense alcohols and phytosterols in rice bran are useful for preventing obesity by regulating the secretion of GIP and SREBP-1c.
rice bran triterpene and sterol components are useful as food additives to prevent obesity.
the triterpene and sterols from the rice bran may have the potential to prevent obesity and diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
triterpens and sterols from natural food resources can be used to develop foods that prevent diet-induced obesity.
the triterpene and sterols from the rice bran may be a good food ingredient for the prevention of obesity.
the oil-solvent components of rice bran are effective in preventing obesity in mice.
